## Data Set


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
data("NHANES")
```
:::


## Taking a Sample

Taking all the Data only from the category [height]{.underline} and then viewing it.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
NHANES_adult <-
  NHANES %>%
  distinct(ID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(Age >= 18) %>%
  select(Height) %>%
  drop_na(Height)
NHANES_adult %>% glimpse()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Rows: 4,790
Columns: 1
$ Height <dbl> 164.7, 168.4, 166.7, 169.5, 181.9, 169.4, 148.1, 177.8, 181.3, …
```


:::
:::


## Population parameters for "Height"

The parameters here being standard deviation and mean.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# NHANES_adult is assumed population
pop_mean <- mosaic::mean(~Height, data = NHANES_adult)
pop_sd <- mosaic::sd(~Height, data = NHANES_adult)
pop_mean
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 168.3497
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
pop_sd
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 10.15705
```


:::
:::


## Sampling

Comparing sample statistics with population parameters on the basis of this ONE sample of 50.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(12345) # for reproducibility
sample_50 <- mosaic::sample(NHANES_adult, size = 50) %>%
  select(Height)
sample_50
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 50 × 1
   Height
    <dbl>
 1   155.
 2   154.
 3   173.
 4   179.
 5   170.
 6   186.
 7   159.
 8   173.
 9   175.
10   170.
# ℹ 40 more rows
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
sample_mean_50 <- mean(~Height, data = sample_50)
sample_mean_50
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 170.094
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
# Plotting the histogram of this sample
ggplot2::theme_set(new = theme_classic())
sample_50 %>%
  gf_histogram(~Height, bins = 10) %>%
  gf_vline(
    xintercept = ~sample_mean_50,
    color = "purple"
  ) %>%
  gf_vline(
    xintercept = ~pop_mean,
    colour = "black"
  ) %>%
  gf_annotate("label",
    y = 7, x = pop_mean - 8,
    label = "Population Mean",
    color = "black"
  ) %>%
  gf_annotate("label",
    y = 7, x = sample_mean_50 + 8,
    label = "Sample Mean", color = "purple"
  ) %>%
  gf_annotate("curve",
    x = sample_mean_50 + 8, y = 6.5,
    xend = sample_mean_50 + 1, yend = 2,
    curvature = -0.2, color = "purple",
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.5, "cm"))
  ) %>%
  gf_annotate("curve",
    x = pop_mean - 8, y = 6.5,
    xend = pop_mean - 1, yend = 2,
    curvature = 0.2, color = "black", arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.5, "cm"))
  ) %>%
  gf_labs(
    y = "Frequency",
    title = "Distribution and Mean of a Single Sample",
    subtitle = "Sample Size = 50"
  )
```
